headline: Foggy, dry Friday, light rain Saturday, then a wetter, windier stretch next week.
summary: A ridge of high pressure aloft is keeping western Washington dry Friday, with fog expected to spread across Puget Sound. By Saturday the ridge is pushed inland as a low drops south from the northeast Pacific and parks offshore through Sunday. That brings light rain to the lowlands and light snow in the mountains, with snow levels near 2,000 feet. Next week a larger low moves in from the Aleutians and deepens offshore Monday night into Tuesday, bringing repeated rounds of rain, mountain snow, and gusty winds. Coastal flooding risk grows on the Pacific coast. Forecasters are fairly confident in the dry start and wetter pattern, but less sure about coastal wind gusts and exact timing. Highs are in the 40s inland.
